\section[despertarse]{despertarse — to wake up}

\label{lesson:ES-C494-despertarse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to suggest, then the Spanish for the doubt.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: despertarse}
\textbf{despertarse} — \textquotedblleft{}to wake up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me despierto a las siete.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I wake up at seven.}
\end{quote}

The e breaks into ie under stress: \emph{me despierto}.

\section[arreglarse]{arreglarse — to get ready, to get dressed up}

\label{lesson:ES-C494-arreglarse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the doubt, then the Spanish for to wake up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: arreglarse}
\textbf{arreglarse} — \textquotedblleft{}to get ready, to get dressed up\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\section[bajar]{bajar — to go down, to come down; to lower}

\label{lesson:ES-C494-bajar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to wake up, then the Spanish for to get ready.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: bajar}
\textbf{bajar} — \textquotedblleft{}to go down, to come down; to lower\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Bajo a comprar el pan.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I go down to buy the bread.}
\end{quote}

The opposite of \emph{subir}. \emph{Bajar el volumen} — to turn the volume down.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: encender}
